NNS Dependence

Source: R/Dependence.R
NNS.dep.Rd

Returns the dependence and nonlinear correlation between two variables based on higher order partial moment matrices measured by frequency or area.

Usage

NNS.dep(x, y = NULL, asym = FALSE, p.value = FALSE, print.map = FALSE)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector, matrix or data frame.

y

NULL (default) or a numeric vector with compatible dimensions to x.

asym

logical; FALSE (default) returns the symmetric measures. If TRUE, returns the asymmetric (directional) measures: the partition is built on x only and the result measures the dependence of y on x (y as a function of x); swap the arguments for the other direction.

p.value

logical; FALSE (default) If TRUE (bivariate only), compares the results against 100 random permutations of y: the Dependence p-value is the upper-tail permutation p-value (1 + #(null >= observed)) / (1 + 100), the Correlation p-value is the two-sided permutation p-value min(1, 2 * min(1 + #(null <= observed), 1 + #(null >= observed)) / (1 + 100)), and the 95 percent intervals of the permutation null are returned (and plotted when print.map = TRUE).

print.map

logical; FALSE (default) Plots quadrant means, or p-value replicates.

Value

Returns the bi-variate "Correlation" and "Dependence" or correlation / dependence matrix for matrix input.

Details

Dependence is a finite-resolution summary of the recursive partitions of NNS.part, which split each cell at the gravity of its observations (noise.reduction = "off"), not at its mean. At each cell, degree-0 (frequency) and degree-1 (area) concordance around the cell means are measured relative to a within-cell permutation reference and rescaled. Their cell-size-weighted averages are evaluated across partition levels. The reported Dependence is the strongest level, floored at zero; Correlation is a signed summary at that selected level and is bounded by Dependence in absolute value. With asym = FALSE, partitions on x, on y, and on joint quadrants are considered. With asym = TRUE, only partitions on x are considered, so the direction describes the resolution supplied by the conditioning variable rather than a causal effect.

The split depth, stopping rules, finite occupancy, and maximization across levels affect the score. A zero score does not prove independence, a noiseless nonlinear function need not score one, and finite independent samples can produce positive scores. The permutation calculation repeats the same selection rule, providing a reference for the selected statistic rather than removing every finite-sample effect from the score itself.

The degree-0 cell reference uses the hypergeometric distribution, with a normal approximation for cell sizes above 400. The degree-1 reference enumerates distinct arrangements only when at most 720 are required (all arrangements for up to six distinct values); larger cells use an approximation. These are properties of the cell calibration, separate from the 100 whole-sample permutations used by p.value = TRUE.

Whole-sample shuffling assumes exchangeability of observations under the null. It is not an automatic test for serially dependent or clustered observations. The returned fields named 95% CIs are central intervals of the permutation null, not confidence intervals for a population dependence parameter. Inclusive-tail counts with the plus-one correction avoid zero Monte Carlo p-values; ties make the test conservative.

Note

For asymmetrical (asym = TRUE) matrices, entry [i, j] is the directional dependence ([row variable i] —> [column variable j]), i.e. NNS.dep(x[, i], x[, j], asym = TRUE), the dependence of column j on row variable i.

References

Viole, F. and Nawrocki, D. (2013) "Nonlinear Nonparametric Statistics: Using Partial Moments" (ISBN: 1490523995, 2nd edition: https://ovvo-financial.github.io/NNS/book/)

Author

Fred Viole, OVVO Financial Systems

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(100) ; y <- rnorm(100)
NNS.dep(x, y)

## Correlation / Dependence Matrix
x <- rnorm(100) ; y <- rnorm(100) ; z <- rnorm(100)
B <- cbind(x, y, z)
NNS.dep(B)
} # }
